variables.reason: The problem's Ra is specified as 'the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations'. The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly defines 'arithmetic mean roughness' (symbols Ra; R_a) as the mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level and lists its SI dimension as L (si_unit: m). This definition is the same statistical quantity named in the problem and directly establishes that Ra carries units of length. The cited record therefore justifies the candidate SI exponents (L=1, all others 0).

The ledger defines kt as 'peak-to-valley height' (vertical distance between highest peak and lowest valley). KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height defines mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols include kt) as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys and lists its SI dimension as L (si_unit: m). The KB definition matches the problem's wording and confirms kt is a length quantity, supporting the candidate exponents (L=1, others 0).

The ledger's k_rms is described as the root-mean-square height. KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines 'root-mean-square roughness height' (symbols k_rms) as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean and specifies SI dimension L (si_unit: m). The KB entry is the canonical match to the problem variable and supports the candidate SI exponents (L=1, others 0).

Sk in the ledger is 'third central moment ... divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height' i.e. standardized skewness. KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (Sk; S_k) as the third standardized moment and explicitly gives si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This is the precise statistical definition used in the problem, so the candidate exponents (all zeros) are confirmed by the KB record.

Ku is given as the kurtosis of height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (Ku; K_u) as the fourth standardized moment and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The KB definition corresponds exactly to the ledger variable and supports the candidate all-zero SI exponents (dimensionless).

ES is defined in the ledger as 'effective streamwise slope'. KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols ES) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This direct KB match justifies the candidate all-zero SI exponents (dimensionless).

Po is described as surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is pores). KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (Po; P_o) as a fraction of void/open volume or area and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The KB entry is the appropriate canonical match and supports the candidate dimensionless SI exponents (all zeros).

variables.quantity_name: First-order absolute moment of height fluctuations
variables.physical_definition: A measure of the average height of surface irregularities from a reference plane.
The vertical distance between the highest peak and the lowest valley in the surface profile.
The square root of the average of the squares of the height fluctuations, representing the roughness of the surface.

variables.quantity_name: Third central moment of roughness height fluctuations
variables.physical_definition: A statistical measure of the asymmetry of the height distribution of surface roughness, normalized by the cube of the root-mean-square height.
A measure of the 'tailedness' of the height distribution of surface roughness, indicating the sharpness of the peak of the distribution.

variables.quantity_name: Effective streamwise slope of the roughness
variables.physical_definition: The average slope of the roughness elements in the direction of the flow, affecting the flow characteristics.

The KB entry is the appropriate canonical match and supports the candidate dimensionless SI exponents (all zeros).

Perform dimensional analysis for sand-grain roughness parameterization to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness (denoted as ks/Ra).

the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations, Ra;
the peak-to-valley height, kt;
the root-mean-square height, k_rms;
the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height, Sk;
the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations, Ku;
the effective streamwise slope of the roughness, ES;
the surface porosity, Po.

variables.quantity_name: First-order absolute moment of height fluctuations
variables.physical_definition: A measure of the average height of surface irregularities from a reference plane.
The vertical distance between the highest peak and the lowest valley in the surface profile.
The square root of the average of the squares of the height fluctuations, representing the roughness of the surface.

variables.quantity_name: Third central moment of roughness height fluctuations
variables.physical_definition: A statistical measure of the asymmetry of the height distribution of surface roughness, normalized by the cube of the root-mean-square height.
A measure of the 'tailedness' of the height distribution of surface roughness, indicating the sharpness of the peak of the distribution.

variables.quantity_name: Effective streamwise slope of the roughness
variables.physical_definition: The average slope of the roughness elements in the direction of the flow, affecting the flow characteristics.
The fraction of the surface area that is occupied by voids or pores, influencing fluid flow and transport.
